label: main season
summary: The survey team’s recorded observation of an object that looked like EO is direct evidence. The second-hand warning is also still unexplained after two visits. National criteria do not provide technical survey, so the target proceeds to clearance for sign-off.
flags: The reported observation is at the edge of the pasture; the team marked and reported the location and took a photo without touching the object.
The desk study places the nearest recorded accident within 1 km, not inside the area; the zone flag and priority are not evidence.

checks.detail: Every item of the evidence log is in the register.
The national criteria provide no technical survey, so clearance takes its place; evidence to target: E1, E2.

E1.quote: A trader passing through the vereda said people should keep away from the area because of mines, but could not say who had seen anything, or where.
E1.note: A vague second-hand warning from an outsider suggests possible contamination but is not based on an identifiable first-hand account.

E2.quote: The survey team saw an object that looked like explosive ordnance on the ground at the edge of the pasture.
E2.note: The team's own recorded observation of an object that looked like EO is direct evidence under the project rule.
